classification.difficultyReason: Same task as the p9-q5 matching question: read the side labels off three drawn shapes, add the perimeter, and recognise the factorised form. The eight-sided shape and the extra count (4a+2b, 3a+3b, 2a+6b) make it slightly more demanding. There are no numeric constants and the HCF is easy to see.

content.prompt:
Match the shapes with the expressions that show their perimeters.

A. $3(a+b)$
B. $2(a+3b)$
C. $2(2a+b)$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P_{\mathrm{i}}&=4a+2b\\P_{\mathrm{i}}&=2(2a+b)\\P_{\mathrm{ii}}&=3a+3b\\P_{\mathrm{ii}}&=3(a+b)\\P_{\mathrm{iii}}&=2a+6b\\P_{\mathrm{iii}}&=2(a+3b)\end{align*}$$
The matches are i–C, ii–A and iii–B.
